name: Air Force Common Admission Test
summary: Officer entry into the Indian Air Force for Flying and Ground Duty (Technical and Non-Technical) branches. Held twice a year. A computer-based test, then the Air Force Selection Board (AFSB) and medicals. Officers start at Level 10.

status.note: AFCAT 1 is usually notified in November with the test in late January or February; AFCAT 2 is notified around May or June with the test in August. AFCAT 01/2026 (340 posts) was notified on 9 November 2025 for courses starting in January 2027.

posts.name: Flying Branch
posts.notes: Up to 26 with a valid commercial pilot licence.

posts.name: Ground Duty (Non-Technical): Weapon Systems, Administration, Accounts, Logistics, Education, Meteorology

age.summary: Flying: 20 to 24 (26 with a commercial pilot licence). Ground Duty: 20 to 26. Age is counted on the course start date.

education.summary: Flying: Class 12 with 50% in Maths and Physics plus a degree with 60% (or BE/BTech 60%). Ground Duty Technical: Class 12 with 50% in Physics and Maths plus a four-year engineering degree. Accounts: B.Com/BBA with 60%. Other branches as per notice.
education.minMarks: 60% in the degree for most branches

eligibility.physical: Air Force medical standards; Flying branch has stricter standards.
eligibility.reservation: Central reservation: SC 15%, ST 7.5%, OBC (non-creamy layer) 27%, EWS 10%, plus horizontal reservation for PwBD and ex-servicemen as per rules.

papers.name: Verbal ability, general awareness, numerical ability, reasoning and military aptitude
papers.negative: Minus 1 for a wrong answer (plus 3 for a right one)

stages.name: Air Force Selection Board (AFSB)
stages.notes: Officer intelligence rating, psychology tests, group tasks and interview. Flying candidates also take the CPSS.

selection.meritCalculation: Merit from AFCAT and AFSB marks among medically fit candidates.
selection.probation: Training at the Air Force Academy and other institutes.

specialAllowances.name: Flying allowance
specialAllowances.detail: For the Flying branch, as per rules.

salary.pension: Defence pension for officers granted Permanent Commission; SSC officers released early do not get a pension.
salary.notes: Flight Lieutenant moves to Level 10B and Squadron Leader to Level 11.

career.promotionNotes: Short Service officers may be considered for Permanent Commission.

benefits.detail: Free medical care, subsidised canteen, quarters, leave travel and group insurance.

workLife.hazards: Moderate to high for flying duties.

difficulty.rationale: Few hundred seats; the AFSB and medicals reject many who clear the test.

ratings.rationale: Two tests every year and officer status from day one.

factors.note: Permanent Commission is not guaranteed for SSC officers.
